analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines ~442-448) and docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~716-749). It describes a new excluded shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The warmup runs once per loaded engine, before the startup calibration probes, in the idle calibration session with the foreground lease, under the same KV and service budgets, and with a 20 s wall budget. It publishes no rates or counters. It also describes a startup-preload pass, and says the periodic MLX pool sweep waits while a session runs. No code is in the supplied evidence, so these claims are unverified.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-010 and T-029 (availability): the warmup could delay or contend with customer work. The docs say it is preemptible via beginForeground. Startup preload warms before registration so routed traffic cannot preempt it, but the documentation says the registration gate's timeout bounds it, and the 20 s budget is bounded.
- A-001 and T-028 (prompt data exposure): the warmup uses synthetic probes, not customer data. The docs claim greedy and default sampling, no cache scope, and no rates trained. Whether the probes populate the SSD prefix cache (T-041) is not stated. A warmup prompt donated to the cache could use the cache scope or the adoption/benefit gates, but that is unverified because no code was supplied.
- The environment variable DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP is a local operator control. It is forwarded by the launchd job and is not coordinator-controlled.

No attestation, authorization, encryption or trust-boundary changes are documented. The nuance is that the MLX pool sweep deferral during warmup is a behavior change in the code, and I cannot check it. A later pass that sees the code should confirm that warmup probes use no customer cache scope, publish no cache receipts and stay out of SSD donation, and that the sweep deferral cannot starve on-pressure reclaim. The docs say on-pressure reclaims still run.
